He's been cleared to return, but Babcock said his plan to wait until the team returns home and faces the Vegas Golden Knights on Tuesday. Nugent-Hopkins has 11 points (four goals, seven assists) in 12 games. items.title: Panthers place Cole Reinhardt on waivers
items.summary: Reinhardt has gone scoreless in three games for Florida this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images A veteran winger has just become available. On Sunday, the Florida Panthers placed forward Cole Reinhardt on waivers. The Calgary native is now eligible to be claimed by any of the other 31 NHL teams. If he clears waivers, the Panthers can assign him to the Charlotte Checkers of the American Hockey League (AHL). Reinhardt, 26, has gone scoreless in three games for Florida this season. He’s also played five games for Charlotte, where he’s put up no goals and two assists. Following his four-year junior career with the Brandon Wheat Kings of the Western Hockey League (WHL), Reinhardt was selected by the Ottawa Senators in the sixth round of the 2020 NHL Entry Draft. In five years with the Senators organization, he played in 18 total NHL games, registering a goal and an assist for two points. He spent most of his time playing for the AHL’s Belleville Senators, including his career-best campaign in the 2022-23 season when he registered 11 goals and 23 assists for 34 points in 66 games. In July of 2025, Reinhardt signed a two-year contract with the Vegas Golden Knights as an unrestricted free agent (UFA). He got his longest look to date at the NHL level in the 2025-26 season, notching three goals and four assists for seven points in 44 games for the Golden Knights. In March of 2026, he was placed on waivers by Vegas and claimed by Florida. He played 15 games for the Panthers to finish off last season, scoring six goals and adding two assists for eight points. items.title: Blackhawks’ Kaiser suspended three games for hit on Flames’ Pospisil
items.summary: Kaiser received a game misconduct for the hit on Saturday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images The NHL Department of Player Safety (DoPS) wasted little time deciding on a punishment for Chicago Blackhawks defenseman Wyatt Kaiser. The NHL DoPS announced on Sunday that Kaiser has been suspended three games for his illegal hit on Calgary Flames forward Martin Pospisil during Chicago’s 4-3 overtime win on Saturday. The hit occured late in the second period when Pospisil was attempting to skate the puck out of his own zone, and Kaiser came across to deliver a direct blow to Pospisil’s head with his shoulder near Calgary’s blueline. Kaiser was assessed a five-minute major and game misconduct for the hit. In a video released by the NHL DPos, it was explained that Kaiser’s hit satisfies both element of the Illegal Check to the Head rule. “First, the head is the main point of contact,” the video states. “Kaiser takes a poor angle of approach and cuts across the front of Pospisil’s body, missing his core and making direct contact with his head. And, it is Pospisil’s head that absorbs the vast majority of the force. While Pospisil is stickhandling and does pull the puck towards his body prior to the check, his head stays level and moves predictably. He does not change the position of his head or body just prior to or simultaneously with contact in a way that significantly contributes to the head being the main point of contact.” Pospisil’s status remains unclear, but he left Saturday’s game and did not return. Kaiser, 24, had not been levied any discipline from the league prior to this suspension. Utah’s leading scorer, Clayton Keller , was unavailable for the matchup against the Anaheim Ducks due to illness . Utah will monitor Keller’s health ahead of Monday’s game against the Winnipeg Jets. The 28 year old is having his best season yet with 29 points in 23 games to start the season. He seems well on track to record a third-consecutive 60-assist season, after posting career-highs with 90 points and 88 points over the last two seasons respectively. The Mammoth have bet on their star accordingly. Keller leads all Mammoth in average ice time (19:12) this season. He also leads the team in power-play ice time, averaging almost four minutes on the man-advantage each game. Keller’s absence left notable holes throughout the Mammoth lineup that led to elevated minutes for Cooley, Kailer Yamamoto , and Barrett Hayton . They will continue to step up if Keller can’t play on Monday. I think Mammoth fans would agree that they could use more goal scoring from Keller. The Colorado Avalanche have a lot of high-end players on the roster, and so when you learn that they have three players with double-digit goal totals at this stage of the season, you couldn't be surprised. But the team leader in goals, with 15, is someone you probably wouldn't have guessed. Artturi Lehkonen has five more goals than either Nathan MacKinnon or Martin Necas, and seven more than Gabriel Landeskog and Brock Nelson. The list goes on, obviously, because he leads the team. More Videos But given the fact that Lehkonen is also a pending UFA - one of just five on the team - this surprising stat takes on greater importance and leads one to ask what might happen here with the team being able to extend him. The good news is that, as things stand now, the Avalanche have about $11.65 million in cap space and, again, only have a handful of free agents to sign. All but Lehkonen should be on the inexpensive side, even with the rapidly rising salary structure across the league. Though he finished without a point — and has yet to record one this season — he had 10 minutes of ice time with three shots on goal. items.body: Explanation: The play on the ice was challenged under Rule 38 – Coach’s Challenge. Rule 38.1 states, “In all Coach’s Challenge situations, the original call on the ice will be overturned if, and only if, a conclusive and irrefutable determination can be made on the basis of video evidence that the original call on the ice was clearly not correct. If a review is not conclusive and/or there is any doubt whatsoever as to whether the call on the ice was correct, the original call on the ice will be confirmed.” After a thorough examination of all available replays, video review determined that Jacob Trouba ’s shot from the defending zone subsequently deflected off Bobby McMann ’s stick before going out of play . The decision was made in accordance with Rule 38.2 (d) which states, in part, that a team may request a Coach’s Challenge “When a minor penalty for delaying the game has been assessed under Rule 63.2 (iii) for shooting or batting the puck out of play from the defending zone. This will only apply to delay of game penalties when the shot/batted puck is determined to have subsequently deflected off a player, stick, glass or boards, etc., and not a judgment call.” Therefore, the delay of game penalty assessed to Jacob Trouba was rescinded.

items.title: Fowler shows he’s human as Canadiens fall to Flyers in final minute
items.summary: Jacob Fowler has already proven he can handle just about anything this league can shoot at him. But on Saturday, the young netminder allowed a late goal that sank the Canadiens against the Flyers.
items.body: MONTREAL — Disappointment burned from Jacob Fowler ’s eyes as he stood in his crease, shaking his head, trying to shake off the goal he’d just surrendered with 31 seconds left in what turned out to be a 4-3 loss for his Montreal Canadiens to the Philadelphia Flyers. It was something we haven’t seen from the young goaltender since he debuted last season, which says everything about who Fowler has been in the NHL. “He’s been our best player,” said Noah Dobson, who was far from being one of Montreal’s better ones in this loss to Philadelphia. Still, the Canadiens were good enough to at least earn a point. They came out of a dominant first tied 1-1, despite Fowler having surrendered one of two shots he faced. They gave up several odd-man rushes in the second and Fowler was beat on more than the one that put the Flyers up 2-1, with shots ringing off the bars behind him before Rasmus Ristolainen made it 3-1 from 60 feet out. And after they played their best hockey of the night in the third, with goals from Zachary Bolduc and Owen Beck coming 74 seconds apart to tie the game, Fowler did something else he never does. He had squared up to Matvei Michkov’s 49-foot, harmless shot, waved his glove at it and, instead of closing it on the puck, deflected it right to Sean Couturier, who scooped up the puck and fed Noah Cates the easiest goal he’ll probably get this season. All Fowler could do after that was watch helplessly as the Canadiens scrambled to tie the game with too little time left on the clock. “He’s human, he’s going to make mistakes,” said Beck, offering up a truth no one should ignore. Least of all Fowler, who’d have probably said he hated that last goal he gave up as much as the first one—even if it was a perfect tip of a wide shot that was virtually impossible to stop.

items.body: Register Login Ducks’ Leo Carlsson Exits With Upper-Body Injury By Gabriel Foley | at November 21, 2026 10:06 pm The Anaheim Ducks lost top center Leo Carlsson to an apparent upper-body injury during Saturday’s matchup with the Utah Mammoth. Carlsson sustained the injury on a hit that sandwiched him between Utah defenseman Mikhail Sergachev and a referee. He was helped off the ice by a trainer. Anaheim announced before the third period that Carlsson would not return. Carlsson became the highest-paid player in the NHL thanks to an offer sheet from the Philadelphia Flyers over the summer. He has followed Anaheim’s historic match with a career-best start to the season. Carlsson has 22 assists and 29 points in 24 games this season, including Saturday night. He has been the setup man to Cutter Gauthier who leads the team with 21 goals and 30 points. In their time together, at all strengths, Carlsson and Gauthier have outscored opponents 32-to-12. They even came together for Anaheim’s opening tally on Saturday, with Gauthier recording the only assist on Carlsson’s seventh goal of the season. The Ducks bumped Mikael Granlund up the lineup in Carlsson’s absence. Granlund could be the ideal playmaker to keep Gauthier’s hot scoring rolling without the Ducks’ star. Named Anaheim’s captain over the summer, Granlund is off to a red-hot start of his own with 26 points in 22 games. He could reach the first 70-point season of his career this year, after passing 60 points five times through 15 seasons in the NHL. items.body: League employees raise nearly $7,000 in fourth edition of charity game MONTREAL -- The employees at the NHL's Montreal office hosted their annual charity ball hockey game at Le Rinque, a sporting complex located in the city's Mount Royal neighborhood on Friday. Thanks to this event, as well as a silent auction held several days prior, the group raised nearly $7,000 ($10,000 in Canadian dollars), which will be donated to the V Foundation as part of the NHL's Hockey Fights Cancer initiative. This was the fourth edition of the ball hockey game, organized by Gianni Fasulo, Jeffrey Martin, Mark Saminaden and Maxime Tellier. The event came into being just prior to the COVID-19 pandemic thanks to the efforts of Saminaden, who was looking for a way to get the Montreal office further involved in the Hockey Fights Cancer initiative. "Everyone knows a family member, a friend or an acquaintance who's dealing with cancer, so this was our way of contributing," said Saminaden. "Mark had set this project in motion, so we wanted to pick up the torch, especially since we didn't really have any other event like this in place," said Fasulo. The ball hockey format was chosen in order to give everyone a chance to take part. After all, since cancer manifests in many different forms, it is only fitting to use every form of hockey to combat it. "There are many more employees who are able to play," said Martin. "Not everyone knows how to skate, and there are even fewer people who play hockey on a regular basis. With ball hockey, the event becomes much more accessible, and those who can't play can still come out and cheer us on." About 20 players took part in this year's event. items.body: BOSTON — Elias Lindholm had the first four-goal game of his NHL career to carry the Boston Bruins past the Washington Capitals 7-5 on Saturday. It was his first hat trick with Boston and the third of his career. David Pastrnak, Tanner Jeannot and Fraser Minten also scored for Boston. Charlie McAvoy added three assists to reach 301 for his career. Minten’s goal was an empty-netter. His fourth goal was on the tip of Pastrnak’s shot that popped over goalie Charlie Lindgren 4:07 into the third, prompting a delayed celebration with many more hats sailing onto the ice as Frankie Valli’s “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You” played over the PA. Lindgren had 16 saves. Back home after ending a three-game losing streak with a victory at Detroit on Wednesday, the Bruins scored three times in the opening nine minutes of the second. items.summary: The hit was egregious, the player was prone and the punishment should be significant. Eric Francis argues why the hit that injured Martin Pospisil deserves a suspension.
items.body: CALGARY — The hit was egregious, the player was prone and the punishment should be significant. In NHL parlance, a one or two-game suspension is significant, and that’s exactly what Wyatt Kaiser should be sentenced to by league disciplinarian George Parros in the next day or two. Forget any debate about intent — every player is responsible for their actions, and in this case the young Chicago Blackhawks defenceman delivered his shoulder to the head of an unsuspecting Martin Pospisil who had his head looking down at the puck along the boards Saturday. As Pospisil reached his own blue line with speed, he attempted a toe-drag of sorts when Kaiser darted at him from the side to deliver a head shot that could have knocked Pospisil out cold. Kaiser received a five-minute major and was booted from the game as a result. It’s the exact type of hit the league has worked so hard to rid the game of, and for good reason. Sadly, supplementary discipline won’t be much of a consolation to the victim, who may once again be staring at another absence from the game. Up until the hit late in the second period of the Flames’ 4-3 overtime loss, Pospisil had been playing the best and most consistent hockey of his career. items.summary: No defenceman is hotter right now than Sam Rinzel as the young Chicago Blackhawks’ blue liner finds himself rubbing shoulders with some of the NHL’s all-time greats.
items.body: No defenceman is hotter right now than Sam Rinzel as the young Chicago Blackhawks ’ blue liner finds himself rubbing shoulders with some of the NHL’s all-time greats. The 22-year-old made it five straight multi-assist games on Saturday with a pair of helpers. He also notched the game-winning goal with 15 seconds left in overtime as Chicago snapped a nine-game road winless skid with a 4-3 victory over the Calgary Flames. Rinzel is the fourth defenceman in NHL history to accomplish that feat, matching five-game runs by Mark Howe (1987-88), Borje Salming (1984-85) and Bobby Orr (1970-71). Rinzel has piled up 12 points (one goal, 11 assists) over the last five games as the Blackhawks have gone 3-1-1 and find themselves playing their finest hockey of the season. “It definitely wasn’t on my bucket list, I can tell you that,” said Rinzel of his recent offensive prowess. “Credit to my teammates, for sure. I’m just playing hockey. I don’t really know. It’s just getting back to not thinking and just playing.” He’ll attempt to extend his streak to six games on Sunday when Chicago’s road trip continues in Vancouver. “Points are funny, they can come and go a little bit, but his play’s been real steady,” said Chicago coach Jeff Blashill. “He’s definitely playing with much more swagger, similar probably to the way he would have in college and in junior.” Rinzel’s dozen points over the past 10 days are just two fewer than his season total last year when he had 14 points in 54 games as a rookie. “He’s playing at a high level,” said veteran Patrick Kane, who also had a goal — set up by Rinzel — and two assists. “Playing at the top on the power play, obviously he’s a righty so we have that one-timer option. We want him to shoot a lot. We want him to get pucks to the net and get chances.”

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Connor Bedard’s 2026 continues to be haunted by one issue. On Saturday, Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson revealed that the Chicago captain will undergo surgery to repair an injury to his right shoulder. Bedard, 21, had surgery on that very same right shoulder on July 8, and was forced to miss the Blackhawks’ first six game this season while in recovery. He re-injured his shoulder during Chicago’s 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs on November 17, when he attempted to take a face-off and immediately left the game. The North Vancouver, British Columbia native is expected to receive the same procedure he underwent in July. No timeline for recovery has been set for Bedard, but he required about three months to recover from that previous surgery. In 15 games played this season, Bedard has seven goals and 11 assists for 18 points . Selected first overall by the Blackhawks in the 2023 NHL Entry Draft, Bedard is in his fourth NHL season. As a rookie in the 2023-24 season, he notched 22 goals and 39 assists for 61 points in 68 games en route to winning the Calder Trophy. His sophomore season of 2024-25 saw him register 23 goals and 44 assists for 67 assists in all 82 games. He had the best year of his career last season, putting up 30 goals and 45 assists for 75 points in 69 games. Bedard is in the first season of a five-year, $75 million contract with Chicago. With 16 points through 23 games this season, the Blackhawks sit in last place in the Central Division , and their -35 goal differential is the second worst in the NHL. items.body: Captain was injured during face-off against Maple Leafs on Tuesday CHICAGO -- Connor Bedard will have surgery on his right shoulder, Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson told traveling reporters following a 4-3 overtime win at the Calgary Flames on Saturday. The 21-year-old captain was injured during a 6-3 win against the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday. He was set to take a face-off against Maple Leafs forward Nick Paul 54 seconds into the third period when, as Bedard put his stick on the ice, Paul’s stick made contact with Bedard’s right hand. He yelled out in pain and immediately went to the locker room. Bedard leads Chicago (7-14-2) with 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 15 games. He scored his seventh goal of the season at 18:51 of the second period on Tuesday, giving the Blackhawks a 3-2 lead. “Obviously we’re thinking about him,” forward Patrick Kane said. “I think he knows how big of a piece he is to this team, what he means to the organization, entertainment value, right, for fans and for the League and what he’s able to provide to the game. So, obviously it’s tough when you’re missing a player like that. “But yeah, just let him know we’re here for him. I’m not sure what the extent of it is and what’s going to happen down the road, but hopefully we can pick him up while he’s out.” It’s the third shoulder injury for Bedard in less than a year. He injured his left shoulder during an offseason training session in Vancouver on July 2 and had surgery a few days later. Bedard was originally expected to be out until November, but he returned on Oct. 13. items.title: Blackhawks’ Connor Bedard to undergo shoulder surgery
items.body: Chicago Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson told reporters Saturday that Bedard will undergo right shoulder surgery later this week after exiting Tuesday's win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. Per Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman, a timeline will be revealed following the operation. Bedard got hurt on a face-off early in the third period against Toronto. The 21-year-old centre slammed his stick on the ice and held his right arm in front of him as he made his way to the locker room. Chicago head coach Jeff Blashill said Thursday that the team was waiting for more information before deciding whether Bedard would have surgery or just rehab the injury. The 21-year-old has a history of shoulder ailments, missing extended time last season with a right shoulder injury and undergoing surgery on his left shoulder in the off-season. Bedard missed the first five Blackhawks games of the season as he rehabbed the injury. The 2023-24 Rookie of the Year had 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 15 games since his return. He became the second-youngest captain in Blackhawks franchise history at the start of the season. Chicago beat the Calgary Flames, 4-3, in overtime earlier Saturday.

items.title: Sam Rinzel’s overtime goal lifts Blackhawks over Flames
items.body: Sam Rinzel scored the overtime winner and had two assists to lead the Chicago Blackhawks past the Calgary Flames 4-3 on Saturday, snapping a nine-game road winless skid. Patrick Kane had a goal and two assists for Chicago (7-14-2). Roman Kantserov and Ryan Donato also scored. The Blackhawks are 3-1-1 in their last five. Ryan Strome, who also had an assist, Jonathan Castagna and Yegor Sharangovich scored for Calgary (10-12-2). Spencer Knight had 32 saves for the visitors. He improved to 7-11-1. Kane’s three points gives the 38-year-old winger 1,415 for his career (510 goals, 905 assists), moving past Doug Gilmour into 22nd on the NHL’s all-time points list. Adam Oates is 21st at 1,420. Blackhawks: Rookie centre Anton Frondell (undisclosed) left the game after two periods due to injury. Kantserov’s 10 goals leads NHL rookies. Chicago went 1-for-2 on the power play to improve to 7-for-14 over the last five games. Flames: Centre Martin Pospisil (upper body) left the game late in the second and did not return after he was elbowed in the head by Blackhawks defenceman Wyatt Kaiser, who was assessed a major penalty and game misconduct. Castagna’s first three NHL goals have come in the last three games. On the ensuing power play after Kaiser’s major penalty, Sharangovich one-timed a Strome pass into the top corner at 1:16 of the third period, tying the score 3-3. Allowing the Flames to pick up a point. With two assists, Rinzel is the first defenceman in Blackhawks history to record multiple assists in five consecutive games. items.body: Register Login Jaroslav Halák Seeking NHL Contract By Josh Erickson | at November 21, 2026 5:55 pm After a few years away from the game, goaltender Jaroslav Halák is looking to make a comeback. His agent, Octagon’s Allan Walsh, said Saturday that Halák is “ determined to play again in the NHL ” after recently suiting up for the Canadiens’ alumni team ahead of the Heritage Classic and responding well to about a month’s worth of training. It would be quite the story to see the 41-year-old return to action. He hasn’t suited up in a competitive game in over three years, last serving as Igor Shesterkin ’s backup with the Rangers in 2022-23. He earned a professional tryout with the Hurricanes the following season but was released without playing a game. He officially announced his retirement last year, but it appears the itch to play never fully went away. Halák is more than willing to begin the comeback journey on an AHL tryout, Walsh said , and is “ not expecting anything to be handed to him .” The Slovak native was a full-time NHL name from 2008 to 2023, aside from a three-month stint in the minors with the Islanders in 2016-17, and was briefly a top-flight option early in his career in lighter workloads. He earned Vezina votes twice — placing 10th with the Canadiens in 2010 and sixth with the Blues in 2012, also taking home the Jennings Trophy that year. Halák put up above-average numbers in 10 of his 17 NHL seasons and was a perfectly passable No. 2 option for his last few years in the league, although he hadn’t been used in any sort of high-leverage way since his outstanding 2019-20 campaign behind Tuukka Rask in Boston. items.body: Explanation: In the final minute of play in the third period and at any point in overtime (regular season and playoffs), the NHL Situation Room will initiate the review of any scenario that would otherwise be subject to a Coach’s Challenge under Rule 38.3. Video review determined that Chicago’s Frank Nazar preceded the puck into the offensive zone and was in an off-side position prior to Roman Kantserov’s goal. items.title: Canucks GM says calls getting Braeden Cootes ready for 2027 World Juniors ‘a priority’ following injury
items.summary: Cootes had two goals with Canada en route to a third-place finish last winter.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Steven Ellis It’s rare for an NHL general manager to outright call the World Juniors “a priority” in a player’s development when they’re already playing pro. But in Braeden Cootes’ case, it might be the best thing for him. During a media availability with Vancouver-based media on Saturday, Vancouver Canucks GM Ryan Johnson addressed Cootes’ lower-body injury. There, he called getting ready for the 2027 World Junior Championship a priority for Cootes, with the 19-year-old expected to be a key part of Canada’s roster in Edmonton. “The World Junior tournament is a priority for me in him being a part of [it],” Johnson said. “So navigating his lower-body injury right now is trying to put him in the best position to get the most out of this season, as we’ve talked about right from training camp. So I fully intend to prioritize making sure he is 100 percent ready to go for the world junior tournament. What the rest of the season looks like after that is something that we’ll address at that time.” While Hockey Canada has left previous participants off the World Junior team in the past, Cootes was expected to be a lock for the tournament. The 19-year-old had two goals in seven games en route to a bronze last year, and then captained Canada in one of the World Junior Summer Showcase games back in July. items.title: Blackhawks’ Kaiser ejected for hit that injures Flames’ Pospisil
items.body: A big hit to the head has cut Martin Pospisil 's game short on Saturday night. The Calgary Flames forward was checked in the head by the Chicago Blackhawks ' Wyatt Kaiser near the end of the second period. Pospisil, who has a history of concussions, fell to the ice and remained there for a few moments before he was helped off and down the tunnel. It was a hard shoulder hit to the head that will likely require a second look from the player safety department. Immediately following the hit, both teams broke into a brawl near the benches. Kaiser was assessed a five-minute major for the hit and a minor penalty for roughing. He was removed from the game and had his penalty served by Ethan Del Mastro. Two roughing penalties were called against Matvei Gridin and Ryan Strome. Pospisil has four goals and six assists through 23 games this season, tied for fifth in points among all other Flames this season. Over his professional hockey career, the 27-year-old has dealt with five reported concussions. The injuries have forced him to consider head injuries differently and focus on recovery, something he opened up about after his last concussion in January.

items.title: Nathan MacKinnon Out Three Months; Cale Makar Out Two Weeks
items.summary: Nathan MacKinnon will miss at least one month while Cale Makar will be out for two weeks due to lower-body injuries.
items.body: Register Login Nathan MacKinnon Out Three Months; Cale Makar Out Two Weeks By Brian La Rose | at November 21, 2026 4:36 pm Nov. 21: Mackinnon’s return timeline has been extended to 12 weeks, head coach Jared Bednar told reporters following Saturday’s practice (via Evan Rawal of The Denver Gazette ). There aren’t any additional details on the nature of his injury, but his timeline was revised after visiting with a specialist and receiving a second opinion, Bednar said. It’s unclear if the additional missed time means MacKinnon elected to undergo surgery for the issue, which appeared to be localized to his lower back or hip. He’s now expected to be out through the All-Star break. MacKinnon already hasn’t suited up since Nov. 12 and went his last two games in the lineup without recording a point. He’s still the team’s scoring leader with a 10-20–30 line through his first 20 games of the season, but will essentially be unavailable for about 40-45% of the Avs’ regular-season games. That’s highly unusual for MacKinnon, whose career-low in games played in a non-shortened season is 64 way back in 2014-15. The Avs have gone 2-0-1 in the early going without their superstar centerman, averaging three goals per game. The league’s second-ranked offense has plenty of depth scoring, but will still be asking a ton of the aging Brock Nelson in the interim as he’s elevated to top-line duties between Artturi Lehkonen and Martin Nečas . items.body: This was a window into what the Edmonton Oilers have still not become this season, despite all the success. Accordingly, the team has brought up some extra depth on the back end, announcing that they’ve recalled Viking Gustafsson Nyberg from AHL Iowa. This is the first recall of the 23-year-old’s career although it won’t be his first taste of NHL action. Gustafsson Nyberg signed with Minnesota late last season as an undrafted college free agent, with the first season of the deal being in 2025-26. Accordingly, that allowed him to make his NHL debut; he got into two games, recording three blocked shots and two hits while averaging over 21 minutes per night. The 27-year-old is off to a great start in his contract year, tallying 34 points in 24 games, a 116-point pace. The team is undoubtedly hoping that his absence won’t be an extended one given how important he is to the Wild as well as the tight Central Division standings race. items.body: Stanley Cup champion receives silver stick before win against Oilers EDM@CAR: Hall honored in pregame ceremony for 1,000 NHL games Taylor Hall received an adorable congratulation video on Saturday. Today, we celebrate Hallsy's 1,000 NHL games with the people who love him most ❤️ pic.twitter.com/vewcGkbDc5 “We just wanted to congratulate you on 1,000 NHL games,” Rachel said in a social media video posted by the team, with Stetson and Chance at her side. “What an amazing accomplishment. “We’re so proud of you,” she continued in the midst of giggles from Stetson. “Thank you for being the best dad and the best husband.” Hall reached the milestone during the Nov.12 NHL Global Series Finland game against the Seattle Kraken. The Cole Harbour, Nova Scotia native is in his 22nd season with the Penguins, and is the franchise’s all-time leader in points (1,775), assists (1,115), and games played (1,441). He has won three Stanley Cups in Pittsburgh, along with two Hart Trophies, two Maurice “Rocket” Richard Trophies, and two Conn Smythe Trophies, along with many other accolades. items.summary: Hughes suffered an injury during Minnesota’s game against the Calgary Flames on Thursday night.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Sorry, Vancouver Canucks fans, you’re just going to have to wait until next season to boo Quinn Hughes a little bit more. When speaking to reporters, Minnesota Wild head coach John Hynes revealed that the talented defenseman will not be in the lineup on Saturday night, when the Wild are expected to visit the Canucks at Rogers Arena. He added that Hughes will not play the final two games of the team’s road trip due to an undisclosed injury, and has returned to St. Paul to be evaluated. Hynes didn’t specify what exactly is ailing Hughes, noting that he wasn’t going to play in the final game of the Wild’s road trip, a matchup with the San Jose Sharks on Monday, regardless of the severity of the injury. Hynes did assure that Hughes isn’t suffering from a concussion. Hughes was hurt during Minnesota’s latest game on Thursday night against the Calgary Flames . Early in the third period, Hughes was shoved hard into the boards by Flames forward Adam Klapka. While the hit seemed innocent, the whiplash of hitting the glass appeared to daze the 27-year-old, leading him to exit the game early. Hughes scored a goal and an assist, logging 23:42 of ice time in a 4-1 victory. Hughes’ injury ends a 13-game point streak, which has seen him score six goals and 21 points over that span. In 24 contests this year, he has posted eight goals and 26 assists for 34 points. He sits second in the NHL in assists and fifth in overall scoring, leading the league with an average TOI of 27:49. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Daniel Kucin Jr.-Imagn Images A familiar face is returning to the Washington Capitals organization. On Saturday, the Capitals reacquired goaltender Clay Stevenson, claiming him off waivers from the Winnipeg Jets . The team subsequently assigned him to its American Hockey League affiliate, the Hershey Bears. Stevenson was originally claimed off waivers by the Jets from the Capitals prior to the start of the 2026-27 season. It came as the Jets were in goaltending limbo following Connor Hellebuyck’s trade request. He ended up playing five games with the Jets, posting a 1-3-0 record with a 3.61 goals-against average and a .870 save percentage. His last appearance came on Nov. 1, when he came in relief of Stuart Skinner, allowing two goals in a 7-0 loss to the Carolina Hurricanes. The undrafted netminder found himself on the outside, looking in, following the Jets trading Hellebuyck to the New Jersey Devils. The Jets acquired netminder Nico Daws as part of the return, one with more significant experience in the NHL. An undrafted netminder out of Dartmouth College, Stevenson joined the Caps organization prior to the 2022-23 season. After spending most of his rookie campaign with the ECHL’s South Carolina Stingrays, the Drayton Valley, Alta. native became one of Hershey’s mainstays between the pipes, helping the team win the Calder Cup during the 2023-24 campaign. Over the previous two seasons, Stevenson appeared in five games with the Caps, going 3-2-0. In 10 career NHL games, Stevenson has a record of 4-5-0, with a 3.08 GAA and an .889 SV%. In 109 regular-season appearances with the Bears, he’s 63-31-9, with a 2.50 GAA, a .909 SV% and nine shutouts. He’s also 4-3, with a 2.38 GAA, a .913 SV% and one shutout in nine postseason contests.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vancouver Canucks will be without star center Elias Pettersson on Saturday night as they host the Minnesota Wild at Rogers Arena, and the game could also go ahead without former captain Quinn Hughes on the visiting blueline. The Canucks confirmed that Pettersson will miss Saturday’s matchup with an upper-body injury, though it is unclear when it occurred, as the Swedish forward played over 22 minutes in Thursday’s 5-1 loss to the Seattle Kraken . Sitting second in team scoring with six goals and 17 assists for 23 points, the now-28-year-old has enjoyed a bounce-back season so far, after scoring just 15 goals and 51 points in 74 games in 2025-26. Outside of his increased offensive contributions, he also has the most shot blocks among all NHL forwards this season, with 32 blocks over 24 games. Vancouver comes into Saturday’s matchup, the first of a back-to-back set, seeking just a second win on home ice in their 11th home game, after a road trip that saw them pick up rare consecutive wins against the Vegas Golden Knights and Utah Mammoth , before falling to the Kraken. It will also mark the second time Hughes is scheduled to return to Rogers Arena after the Canucks traded him to the Wild in a blockbuster deal 11 months ago. While Hughes had to leave Minnesota’s last game against the Calgary Flames , there were no updates on his condition as of Saturday morning. Once the final buzzer sounds between the Canucks and Wild, Vancouver will turn its attention to a Sunday clash with the Chicago Blackhawks , which won’t feature Blackhawks star center and North Vancouver native Connor Bedard due to a shoulder injury suffered while taking a faceoff earlier in the week against the Toronto Maple Leafs .

items.body: The Vancouver Canucks are juggling their roster ahead of a back-to-back this weekend. Brendan Gallagher has been placed on the injured reserve with a lower-body injury, and forwards Ty Mueller and Jacob Quillan and goaltender Nikita Tolopilo have been recalled from the American Hockey League, the team announced Saturday. Gallagher's placement on the IR is retroactive to Nov. 19, when he suffered the injury in a 5-1 loss to the Seattle Kraken. Gallagher has three points in 20 games this season for the Canucks. Meanwhile, Mueller will be in line for his first taste of NHL action this season, should he lace up for the Canucks. The 23-year-old was drafted by the Canucks in the fourth round in 2023 and has one goal in eight appearances at the NHL level in the prior two seasons. Quillan, 24, last suited up for Vancouver on Nov. 5, recording his first and only point with the team in three games this year. He has five goals and two assists in seven games with Abbotsford. Tolopilo, 26, played well in his lone appearance for the Canucks this year, a 3-2 win over the Utah Mammoth on Nov. 16. Over his three seasons in the NHL, he has a 3.44 goals-against average and .885 save percentage in 24 games played (20 starts). items.title: Line brawl breaks out between Michigan, Michigan State
items.body: There is no love lost between the University of Michigan and Michigan State hockey teams. A line brawl broke out on Friday night between the intra-state rivals — a rarity in college hockey, where the NCAA strictly prohibits fighting across all sports, including hockey. The melee started when Michigan State defenceman Sean Barnhill laid a hit from behind on Michigan forward and Toronto Maple Leafs prospect Nick Moldenhauer. Multiple fights ensued with members of the Michigan State penalty box skating out to join in on the fracas. In total, a combined 71 penalty minutes were handed out, including five major penalties and four disqualifications. Per the NCAA prohibition on fighting, a disqualification results in an automatic one-game suspension. Players facing the ban include Barnhill, Nick Sima, Drew Shock and Montreal Canadiens prospect Michael Hage. Time will tell if a rematch is in order or if cooler heads will prevail, as the two teams face each other again on Saturday night.

items.body: Teammates cheer on forward in AHL rehab assignment in recovery from hip surgery BROSSARD, Quebec -- Jonathan Huberdeau received the best possible show of affection for his return to hockey on Wednesday after having a left hip resurfacing operation in March. In his first game with the Calgary Wranglers in the American Hockey League, Huberdeau played in front of several of his Calgary Flames colleagues, as well as under the watchful eye of Flames coach Ryan Huska. "It really warmed my heart. I was so touched to see my teammates there," said Huberdeau. They've still got my back, they're rooting for me to get healthy again. I didn't think there would be so many of them." Thompson, arguably the team’s best player over the last two seasons, has looked little like his former self this month. In seven starts since November 1, Thompson has allowed an average of 3.4 goals per game for just a .841 save percentage, giving up goals on opponents’ first shot of the game three times in under three weeks. Head coach Spencer Carbery pulled Thompson just once in his first 110 games for Washington; he’s now done so twice in six games. As the Capitals look to snap Thompson out of his funk, they have two options. They could opt to keep playing Thompson, getting him back on the horse as soon as possible. Or they could start Charlie Lindgren , giving Thompson time to reset before going back in the net. “We haven’t made a decision on what’s going to go on for tomorrow night,” Carbery said. “There’s some times where you just want to let a guy play through some struggles, and then there’s sometimes where you’d like him to take a step back. “Both can be utilized and both are appropriate at given times, and that’s just up to (goaltending coach) Scotty Murray, Logan, myself, and making the best decision possible.” The pros and cons of each approach go beyond a single game. According to a team announcement , the Vancouver Canucks traded forward Max Sasson to the Rangers for a 2029 fourth-round pick. It’s the third notable trade between the Rangers and Canucks since January of 2025, when Vancouver sent forward J.T. Miller to the Big Apple. The Birmingham, MI, native spent his collegiate days with the Western Michigan University Broncos before Vancouver signed him after his 2022-23 season. Sasson finished his two-year tenure in Kalamazoo with 24 goals and 64 points in 75 games. He had an easy jump to the professional ranks. Throughout his first season with the Abbotsford Canucks in the AHL, Sasson scored 18 goals and 42 points in 54 games with a +14 rating. Debuting in the NHL a year later, Sasson helped Abbotsford win the Calder Cup after scoring five goals and 14 points in 24 postseason contests. The 2025-26 season marked his first full NHL season. items.title: Canucks trade Max Sasson to Rangers for fourth-round pick
items.body: With the entire NHL having a night off, the Vancouver Canucks and New York Rangers made a small move. The Canucks traded forward Max Sasson to the Rangers in exchange for a 2029 fourth-round pick, the teams announced on Friday. The centre netted eight points (five goals, three assists) in 24 games to start the season for Vancouver. Sasson signed with the Canucks as a free agent out of Western Michigan University in 2023 and split his time between the NHL and AHL, including winning the Calder Cup with Abbotsford in 2025. The Michigan native scored 34 points (21 goals, 13 assists) in 119 games for the Canucks in the NHL over parts of three seasons. Sasson could join the Rangers lineup as soon as Sunday afternoon, when they take on the Carolina Hurricanes at home at 12:30 p.m. ET on Sportsnet+.

items.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs' season is hanging by a thread, largely due to the play of Sergei Bobrovsky. But one NHL goalie analyst says this situation could've been avoided.

According to Steve Valiquette, who said he sent a report to GM John Chayka in the summer warning of Bobrovsky's long-term decline, the decision was totally avoidable. "He was a minus-22 (goals saved above expected)," Valiquette, a former NHL goalie who is now an analyst with MSG Network and the CEO of Clear Sight Analytics, told The Hockey News' Big Show on Friday. "What we've found over the last 12 years at Clear Sight is that at age 38, that's the major decline risk signal," he said. "And for older goalies, minus-15 is often the beginning of structural decline. Once older goalies fall below that minus-15 line, recovery becomes much less likely at this age. items.title: Nemec gets unlikely assist from Flames equipment manager Ben Dumaine
items.summary: here aren’t many equipment managers who get to celebrate a highlight-reel assist, get a shoutout on Sportsnet and have an NHL defenceman searching for a fine bottle of wine for them.
items.body: CALGARY — There aren't many equipment managers who get to celebrate a highlight-reel assist, get a shoutout on Sportsnet and have an NHL defenceman searching for a fine bottle of wine for them. Ben Dumaine managed all three Thursday night, thanks to a quick reaction that helped Simon Nemec turn a broken stick into a beautiful goal. After going viral with the stick fix, the 37-year-old Flames assistant equipment manager arrived at the Saddledome Friday morning a bashful celebrity of sorts. “Joel Hanley came up to me and said, ‘You’ve got more assists than I do this year,'" chuckled the popular dressing room assistant. It's a pretty unique accomplishment for a guy whose usual highlights involve skate sharpeners, laundry and equipment bags. Nemec had his stick slashed in half in his own zone Thursday against Minnesota, and while approaching the bench with speed, he contemplated a change when he spotted Dumaine holding out his backup. He grabbed it on the fly, kept going up ice and turned a two-on-one into a three-on-one. Morgan Frost delivered a slick pass, and Nemec one-timed it home. “I might get him a bottle of wine or something,” said Nemec, dubbing it a “pretty sick goal.” “I mean, he was a big part of that. Benny did a good job. He had the stick ready for me and I had pretty good speed, so I used that and it went in.” Here's the best part: Dumaine didn't see the stick break, never saw the goal, and had no idea what an integral role he played in it. It was his boss, equipment manager Mark DePasquale, who spotted the broken stick and yelled out “71,” Nemec's jersey number. Dumaine instinctively grabbed the replacement from the nearby stick rack and held it out as Nemec approached. items.body: Register Login Transaction Notes: Beckman, Gagne, McWard, Clendening By Brennan McClain | at November 20, 2026 5:01 pm The Colorado Avalanche trimmed down their active roster after last night’s win over the Anaheim Ducks. According to a team announcement , the Avalanche assigned forward Adam Beckman and defenseman Alex Gagne to the Colorado Eagles in the AHL. Odds are, one of Beckman and Gagne will return for the Avalanche’s upcoming contest. Colorado has a five-day break until their next game, and with the Eagles playing tonight and tomorrow, it leaves Beckman and Gagne plenty of time to meet their call-up requirements. Of the two, only Beckman played against the Ducks last night. He went scoreless in 8:32 of ice time. Meanwhile, Gagne has appeared in two games for Colorado during his recall, going scoreless in both contests while delivering six hits. Given the Avalanche’s multiple injuries and the lack of returns anytime soon, it wouldn’t be surprising if both Beckman and Gagne were back on the roster by next Wednesday.

items.title: How much should team quality impact a goalie’s Vezina candidacy?
items.summary: Some goaltenders are great on their own, but their stock might be elevated based on the team in front of them.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images The process for determining who wins the Vezina Trophy as the NHL’s top goaltender has been heavily debated for eons. Along with whether general managers should be the ones voting on the award, the criteria for what makes a goaltender the best in the league is another hot topic. For most of its history, goaltenders seemingly only qualify for the award if their team makes it to the Stanley Cup Playoffs, though Sergei Bobrovsky took home the honor on a Columbus Blue Jackets team that failed to make it to the postseason. On Friday’s edition of Daily Faceoff LIVE, Tyler Yaremchuk and Carter Hutton discuss whether a goaltender is a true Vezina contender if the team in front of him is good. Tyler Yaremchuk: [Pyotr] Kochetkov…not considered one of high-end goalies in the NHL. But these numbers are absolutely insane. But what a lot of people will say is, ‘Well, yeah, he plays on Carolina. That’s a team that limits chances and all this stuff.’ How much do you factor in the quality of the team in front of the goalie when kind of picking out and trying to pick your way through this Vezina conversation. Carter Hutton: It’s not a non-factor, right? It’s something to go into that, but it’s also something you don’t control, too. items.title: Former NHLer Jesse Puljujarvi releases song ‘Is It Time?’
items.summary: Puljujarvi collaborated with Finnish artist Samuell on the song.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: USA TODAY Sports NHL fans might remember Jesse Puljujarvi as a winger, but now, it’s time to get to know him as a singer. The former Edmonton Oilers forward has released a song called “Is It Time?” with Finnish artist Samuell. The lyrics of the song are all in Finnish except for the chorus, which repeats the refrain “Is It Time?” after some catchy “whoa-whoa-whoas” . It’s an upbeat, electro-dance record, and the cover art for the song features Puljujarvi’s Finnish national number-13 jersey hung next to a custom-made Finnish number-23 jersey with “SAMUELL” on the name plate. According to a profile on the Team Agency website , Samuell’s song “Hei Supermario” released in March became popular on TikTok and garnered him national attention in Finland. He makes music which “stands out for its harmonies, straightforward lyrics, and uninhibited attitude.” This is the first indication of any musical inclination for Puljujarvi, who currently plays for Genève-Servette HC in the Swiss National League, where he’s notched six goals and 12 assists for 18 points in 18 games so far this season. Selected fourth overall by the Oilers in the 2016 NHL Entry Draft, Puljujarvi also played for the Carolina Hurricanes , Pittsburgh Penguins , and Florida Panthers before signing with Genève-Servette HC ahead of the 2025-26 season.
